lectures.title: Time and Space Complexity of Queue using Array

cues.en: All right.
In this lecture we are going to look at big picture of time and space complexity of Q using array.
Now the first method is n q method.
On average the time complexity for n q method is going to be O1, and we know that for n q method,
we are using the push method of the array, which typically has a constant time complexity.
However, in the worst case scenarios, when the underlying array needs to be resized, it can be on.
Now the space complexity is o one, because when we are enqueuing the element, we are enqueuing only
one element, so an additional memory is not required to perform this operation.
Now the next method is the Q method.
So when we are dequeuing the elements from the q, we are removing the first element of the underlying
array, which means that all elements has to shift one step left.
That's why this is going to take all n time complexity.
Now the space complexity here again is o one, because here again we are just removing one element.
So an additional memory is not required.
Then the next method is front method which is returning the first element from the queue.
So this means that we are going to access the first elements in the underlying array.
So we know that accessing the element using the index is going to take all one time complexity.
So the space complexity is also O one.
Then we have Isempty method.
In Isempty method, we are just checking that if the array is empty or not.
So this method simply checks the length of the array, which is a constant time operation, and the
space complexity is also o one.
Because an additional memory is not required, then we have size method.
So size method is a direct access to the length property of the array.
This will take O one time complexity and it does not use any extra space.
That's why the space complexity is o one when it comes to the clear method.
Here we are just setting the array to the empty array.
That's why the time and space complexity is going to be o one.
So this is the big picture of time and space complexity of Q operations using array implementation.
So hopefully everything is clear.
